en: Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 8.19. The Dyad of Being Dissociated from the Taints and Having Taints (Āsavavippayutta-sāsava-duka)

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*) and is not itself a taint, there arises a state dissociated from the taints and not itself a taint, by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints and not itself a taint, there arises a state dissociated from the taints but which is a taint, by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints and not itself a taint... [there arises] a state dissociated from the taints... by way of root condition.
States that are dissociated from the taints and are not non-tainted arise by way of the root condition:
depending on a state dissociated from the taints and not non-tainted, a state dissociated from the taints and not non-tainted arises by way of the root condition;

depending on states both dissociated from the taints and not non-tainted, and dissociated from the taints and not non-tainted, a state dissociated from the taints and not non-tainted arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two ... [and so on] ... in the non-disappearance condition, there are five. (The detailed exposition applies to all cases.
The section on the taints is concluded.
